name: CWF-Pro Canadian Title
epitaph: Opened December 1997 as the CWF-Pro Canadian Heavyweight Title (renamed CWF-Pro Canadian Title by March 1998), when Mike Hart won a tournament final over Ticking Time Bomb to become its 1st Canadian Champion. Across 81 recorded reigns White Zombie (6), Mr. Universe (4) and Jimmy Lee (4) return most often, and a long run of its own title changes double as unification nights — rival promotions' own belts, from the TPW United States Title to the CWE Canadian Title, folded into it one by one as CWF-Pro absorbed each fed's own top titles. The Golden One closes the ledger's own account in December 2007, unifying it together with the Royal Title into the Intercontinental Title in a 3-way dance. 22 of the 81 recorded holders (27%) survive only as bare ledger names.

name: CWF-Pro Crown
epitaph: Founded April 1997 alongside CWF-Pro's other flagship belts, when Jackson won a battle royal eliminating Beastman to become the 1st CWF-Pro King — the ledger's own first line also records a short-lived coup, the Vice President stealing and self-crowning the belt before Pres Burns restored it to Jackson and released the Vice President. Hammerman, Wasp and Lost Soul are its only two-time champions across 21 recorded reigns; one reign ended when Machine of War was injured, another when the Icon Miguel Sanchez was suspended. Muhammad Cala closes the ledger's own account in October 2007, defeating the Golden One to unify the Crown with the Royal Title — the ledger records the Crown itself as “no longer used” from that reign on.

name: CWF-Pro Title
epitaph: Opened April 1997 as the CWF-Pro World Heavyweight Title (renamed the CWF-Pro Title that December), when the Icon Miguel Sanchez won a battle royal eliminating Gator at the fed's own “2nd TNF” to become its 1st CWF-Pro World Champion, unifying three developmental belts (UBH, AIWA, DBWF) into it the same night. Across 143 recorded reigns Mike Powers (22), Sanchez (18) and Beastman (14) dominate the ledger, and dozens more changes each fold in a rival promotion's own top belt — the EWF, UCWF, WWWWF, IWWA, IWF, NWO and AWI World Titles among many others — as the belt absorbed CWF-Pro's acquired predecessors and in-house developmental leagues one by one. The ledger's own printed numbering carries two genuine irregularities, preserved exactly as the source prints them: two reign changes are marked “X” instead of a sequential number — one restores Major Disorder to the belt while reprinting his own earlier “(2)” reign-count suffix rather than advancing it, the other restores Seven — and two further numbers, 49 and 133, are simply missing from the fed's own printed list. Eric Michaels holds the belt at the ledger's own last recorded line; 16 of the 143 recorded champions survive only as bare ledger names.
notes: CWF-Pro's own served title-history ledger records 143 reigns in full; all 143 are structured into data/reigns.json — see promotions/cwfpro/archive/cwf-pro-title.html for the underlying primary source.

epitaph: Opened July 2007 for the WWW women's brand, when Hot Baby won a battle royal eliminating Shannon Gill to become its 1st Bytch Champion. Beth Nasty (4) and Shannon Gill (3) are its most frequent holders across 19 recorded reigns, nearly three-quarters of them otherwise bare ledger names. Amber Burns closes the ledger's own account, defeating the Domatrix to unify the WWW Bytch Title with the CWF-Pro Women's World Title.

name: WWW World Tag Team Title
epitaph: Opened July 2007 for the WWW women's brand, when the Davis Girls (Ashley & Amber Davis) won a battle royal eliminating the Spoiled Brats to become its 1st WWW World Tag Team Champions.
